To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
program-level adaptive memory management can provide up to a factor 7.8 speedup for real-world Java programs.
program-level heap size adaptation is an effective approach to improving the performance of Java programs.
program-level adaptive heap control provides significant performance benefits for applications running on virtual machines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to manage the memory of a Java application to achieve optimal performance.
the problem of adaptive heap control.
the question: how can we best use the available memory in a system? We show that the answer to this question is highly application dependent.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed adaptive heap size scheme is effective and efficient in improving performance of Java applications.
the adaptive scheme outperforms all other schemes for all applications, except for the case where the fixed heap size is set to the best possible value.
the program-level heap control scheme is effective for a variety of applications and is a viable alternative to the current heap size selection scheme.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adaptive heap size control is effective for a wide variety of applications.
adaptive memory management is an important technique that should be incorporated into the design of all virtual machines.
our adaptive memory management scheme is effective in reducing the overall runtime of applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a good heap size for a program depends on its memory usage and the number of page faults it incurs.
the optimal heap size varies across applications and across different garbage collectors.
the optimal heap size is not a constant, but a function of the application's memory usage and the underlying system configuration.
